name: 40 Hz gamma, magnetic sine (GENUS rate only)
origin: Rhythm from the Tsai lab's GENUS light and sound flicker (MIT Picower Institute; Cognito Therapeutics trials); the magnetic version is a project construct
summary: A 40 Hz sine field (50 points per cycle) on all eight ring coils in phase for 1 h, the smooth version of lowfield-gamma-40hz-square. From GENUS, the Tsai lab's 40 Hz light and sound flicker, it takes only the rate and the 1 h length. A magnetic 40 Hz field is this project's own design: no source describes one, and it has no evidence.
notes: GENUS (gamma entrainment using sensory stimuli) is a light flickering at 40 Hz, '12.5 ms light on, 12.5 ms light off', for 1 h (Iaccarino 2016 l.143). Martorell 2019 added a 1-ms 10 kHz tone every 25 ms, 'coupled with' the light pulses (l.123), 1 h a day. No source describes a magnetic 40 Hz exposure. This program plays a 40 Hz sine with 50 points per cycle (0.5 ms each) on the full ring, all coils in phase. A sine copies only the 40 Hz rate and the 1 h length, not the on/off flicker; the on/off version is lowfield-gamma-40hz-square. Light and sound are left out: they would need new hardware (a GPIO-driven LED and I2S audio on the ESP32), so the part of GENUS that has data is missing here. The sources state no field strength, because they use light and sound; the 5 uT is this project's choice. This program's setting is the peak field 20 mm in front of each coil. A magnetic 40 Hz field has no evidence. The sensory results are themselves contested: Soula 2023 found no gamma entrainment or amyloid change from 40 Hz light in mice, the human data are small trials (e.g. Chan 2022), and a meta-analysis (Ang 2025) found no established cognitive benefit. This program is not a treatment for Alzheimer's disease or any other condition. If you add 40 Hz light flicker from another device, screen for photosensitive epilepsy first and offer a sound-only mode; the same meta-analysis raised a tinnitus signal for the sound. Not for people with epilepsy; stop on headache or distress.
setting: Seated and relaxed, eyes open or closed, in a quiet room.
schedule: The GENUS studies used 1 h a day (Chan et al. 2022: daily for 3 months). No schedule has been tested for a magnetic 40 Hz field.
source: Iaccarino et al. 2016, Nature 540:230 https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5656389/ ; Martorell et al. 2019, Cell 177:256 https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6774262/ ; Soula et al. 2023, Nat Neurosci https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10839995/ ; Chan et al. 2022, PLoS One https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9714926/ ; Ang et al. 2025, meta-analysis https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12700959/
